mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer discretionary spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 1400K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 4.0% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, a tightening labor market drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as firms increase investments.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average signals a pickup in economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as manufacturers' profits rise.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO surpasses its 6-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annual growth rate (GDPC1) below 2.0% indicates slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as investors reassess growth prospects.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP growth and stock market performance
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth is below 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2.0% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth is above 3.0%, a hawkish monetary stance combined with rising inflation leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher rates reduce borrowing.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a labor market shock, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as investors react to the surprise.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market shocks and stock reactions
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent growth in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average, indicating strong consumer spending, leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as retailers' profits increase.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS growth is consistently above its 3-month MA.
